title: Cardiac review of symptoms
goal: Run a full cardiac review of symptoms: chest pain, breathlessness, swelling, palpitations, dizziness and fainting, and how far the patient can walk.

grammar.p: Many symptoms use the *gustar* pattern: the symptom is the subject and the person is *me / le*. *Me falta el aire* is literally 'air is lacking to me'. The verb agrees with the symptom: *me duele la pierna* but *me duelen las piernas*. For swelling, patients say *se me hinchan los pies* (my feet swell); you ask *¿Se le hinchan los pies?*
ex: ¿Le falta el aire cuando camina?
Are you short of breath when you walk?
¿Se le hinchan los tobillos en la tarde?
Do your ankles swell in the afternoon?
Me duelen las pantorrillas cuando camino.
My calves hurt when I walk.

grammar.h: Triggers: al + infinitive, cuando, en reposo
grammar.p: To ask what brings a symptom on, use *al* + infinitive (*al caminar* = when walking) or *cuando* + present (*cuando sube escaleras*). Contrast *con el esfuerzo* (with exertion) and *en reposo* (at rest). *Hasta* means 'even': *hasta en reposo* = even at rest.
ex: ¿Le falta el aire al subir escaleras?
Do you get short of breath climbing stairs?
¿Le da dolor de pecho con el esfuerzo?
Do you get chest pain with exertion?
Me falta el aire hasta en reposo.
I'm short of breath even at rest.

grammar.h: The fainting story: imperfect for the scene, preterite for the event
grammar.p: Use the imperfect for the background (where the patient was, what they were doing, what it was like): *estaba, hacía, había*. Use the preterite for what happened: *me mareé, me desmayé, me caí, me golpeé*. A closed period with a measured length also takes the preterite: *¿Cuánto tiempo estuvo inconsciente?*
ex: ¿Qué hacía cuando se desmayó?
What were you doing when you fainted?
Estaba en la iglesia y hacía mucho calor.
I was in church and it was very hot.
Me mareé, se me nubló la vista y me caí.
I got dizzy, my vision went dim, and I fell.

grammar.p: Measure function with *cuadras* (blocks), *pisos* (floors) and *escaleras* (stairs). Compare with the past using the imperfect for 'used to': *Antes caminaba diez cuadras; ahora camino dos.* *Podía* = 'I used to be able to'.
ex: ¿Cuántas cuadras puede caminar sin parar?
How many blocks can you walk without stopping?
Antes subía tres pisos sin problema.
I used to climb three floors without a problem.
Ahora me canso más que antes.
Now I get tired more than before.

grammar.p: Patients describe the heartbeat as *rápido* (fast), *acelerado* (racing), *fuerte* (pounding), *irregular*, or as *brincos* (skips, jumps). Here *lo* means 'it' (the heart): *¿Lo siente rápido?* = Do you feel it fast?
ex: ¿Siente el corazón rápido, fuerte o irregular?
Do you feel your heart fast, pounding, or irregular?
Siento brincos en el pecho.
I feel skips in my chest.
El corazón me late muy rápido.
My heart beats very fast.

items.q: How do you ask a patient 'Are you short of breath when you walk?'
items.why: Usted with patients (le … camina); aire is masculine (el aire); present tense for a general symptom.

items.q: A patient says: «Duermo con tres almohadas porque acostado me falta el aire.» Which symptom is this?
items.why: Needing several pillows because lying flat causes breathlessness = orthopnea.

items.q: ¿Cuántas ___ usa para dormir?
items.qen: How many pillows do you use to sleep?
items.why: Pillow = la almohada. Cobija = blanket, sábana = sheet.

items.q: Me desmayé mientras ___ la cena.
items.qen: I fainted while I was making dinner.
items.why: Mientras + the background action in progress → imperfect: preparaba.

items.q: You want to know whether anyone saw the patient faint. Which question asks that?
items.why: Alguien (someone) is the subject; a finished event → preterite vio … pasó.

items.q: A patient says: «Siento brincos en el pecho.» What does she mean?
opts: She has burning in her chest.
She feels her heart skipping or jumping.
She has a stabbing chest pain.
items.why: Brincos (jumps) is a common way to describe skipped or extra beats.

items.q: Antes ___ veinte cuadras sin parar; ahora solo camino dos.
items.qen: I used to walk twenty blocks without stopping; now I only walk two.
items.why: 'Used to' (a past habit) → imperfect: caminaba.

items.q: Cuando me desmayé, ___ en la iglesia.
items.qen: When I fainted, I was in church.
items.why: Where the patient was is background to the event → imperfect: estaba.

items.q: Which word means 'ankles'?
items.why: Tobillos = ankles. Rodillas = knees, pantorrillas = calves, talones = heels.

items.q: A patient says: «Cuando camino me duelen las pantorrillas, y el dolor se me quita cuando descanso.» This history suggests:
items.why: Calf pain brought on by walking and relieved by rest = claudication.

items.q: How do you ask a patient 'Do you get dizzy when you get up?'
items.why: Usted form, present tense for a recurring symptom; levantarse = get up (acostarse = lie down).

items.q: ¿Le falta el aire ___ subir escaleras?
items.qen: Do you get short of breath when you climb stairs?
items.why: Al + infinitive = when/while doing something: al subir.

items.q: How do you ask 'Do you wake up at night short of breath?'
opts: ¿Se duerme en la noche con falta de aire?
¿Se despierta en la noche con falta de aire?
¿Despierta usted a alguien en la noche?
¿Se despertó en la noche con falta de aire?
items.why: Despertarse = to wake up; present tense for a recurring symptom. Dormirse = to fall asleep.

items.q: After a faint, how do you ask 'Did you hit your head?'
items.why: One finished event → preterite; golpearse is reflexive (se golpeó) and Spanish uses la with body parts.

items.q: A patient says: «Siento el corazón muy acelerado.» What does she mean?
opts: My heart feels like it's racing.
My heart feels like it stopped.
items.why: Acelerado = racing, sped up.

items.q: How do you ask 'How many blocks could you walk a year ago?'
opts: ¿Cuántas cuadras puede caminar hace un año?
¿Cuántas cuadras podía caminar hace un año?
¿Cuántas cuadras podrá caminar hace un año?
¿Cuántas cuadras pudo caminar en un año?
items.why: Ability back then, as a general state → imperfect podía. 'En un año' would mean 'in (the course of) a year'.

items.q: ¿Cuántos ___ puede subir sin parar?
items.qen: How many floors can you climb without stopping?
items.why: Piso = floor/story. Cuadras is feminine (cuántas) and means blocks; pasos = steps.

items.q: Tengo los tobillos ___.
items.why: Los tobillos is masculine plural → hinchados.

items.q: ¿Sintió algo ___ desmayo?
items.qen: Did you feel anything before the faint?
items.why: Antes de + el desmayo → antes del desmayo (de + el contracts to del).

items.q: A patient says: «Me falta el aire hasta en reposo.» What does that tell you?
opts: She is short of breath only with exercise.
She is short of breath only lying down.
She is short of breath even at rest.
She is no longer short of breath.
items.why: Hasta = even; en reposo = at rest.

items.q: ¿Le ___ el aire cuando sube escaleras?
items.en: Do you get short of breath when you climb stairs?
items.why: Gustar pattern: el aire is the subject → falta.

items.q: ¿Cuántas ___ usa para dormir?
items.en: How many pillows do you use to sleep?
items.why: Pillow = almohada (feminine, so cuántas).

items.q: Ayer me ___ en el baño.
items.en: Yesterday I fainted in the bathroom.
items.why: A finished event yesterday, yo → preterite desmayé.

items.q: ¿Qué ___ usted cuando se desmayó?
items.en: What were you doing when you fainted?
items.why: What was going on in the background → imperfect hacía (or estaba haciendo).

items.q: ¿Cuánto tiempo ___ inconsciente?
items.en: How long were you unconscious?
items.why: A closed period with a measured length → preterite estuvo.

items.q: Tengo los pies muy ___.
items.en: My feet are very swollen.
items.why: Los pies is masculine plural → hinchados.

items.q: Antes ___ diez cuadras; ahora solo camino dos.
items.en: I used to walk ten blocks; now I only walk two.
items.why: 'Used to' → imperfect caminaba.

items.q: ¿___ pisos puede subir sin parar?
items.en: How many floors can you climb without stopping?
items.why: Piso is masculine → cuántos, with an accent because it is a question word.

items.q: ¿Siente que el corazón le ___ muy rápido?
items.en: Do you feel that your heart is beating very fast?
items.why: El corazón (it) → late. (Está latiendo is also correct.)

items.q: ¿Le duelen las piernas ___ caminar?
items.en: Do your legs hurt when you walk?
items.why: Al + infinitive = when doing something.

items.q: ¿Alguien ___ lo que pasó?
items.en: Did anyone see what happened?
items.why: Alguien (he/she form), finished event → preterite vio (no accent).

items.q: Mientras ___ la cena, sentí el corazón muy rápido.
items.en: While I was making dinner, I felt my heart racing.
items.why: Mientras + background action → imperfect preparaba (or estaba preparando).

items.q: ¿Se ___ la cabeza cuando se cayó?
items.en: Did you hit your head when you fell?
items.why: Usted, a finished event → preterite golpeó.

items.q: ¿Se le ___ los tobillos en la tarde?
items.en: Do your ankles swell in the afternoon?
items.why: Los tobillos is the subject (plural) → se le hinchan.

items.q: Anoche me ___ a las tres de la mañana con falta de aire.
items.en: Last night I woke up at three in the morning short of breath.
items.why: Anoche + one event → preterite desperté.

items.q: ¿Le da dolor de pecho ___ hace esfuerzo?
items.en: Do you get chest pain when you exert yourself?
items.why: Cuando + present for a recurring situation.

items.q: Me siento muy ___ todo el día.
items.en: I feel very tired all day. (a woman speaking)
items.why: A woman speaking → feminine cansada.

items.q: ¿El dolor ___ cuando descansa?
items.en: Does the pain go away when you rest?
items.why: Quitarse = to go away (pain): el dolor se (le) quita.

items.q: Antes ___ subir tres pisos sin problema.
items.en: I used to be able to climb three floors without a problem.
items.why: 'Used to be able to' (general past ability) → imperfect podía.

items.q: ¿Hace cuánto ___ los mareos?
items.en: How long ago did the dizzy spells start?
items.why: Los mareos (plural) is the subject; when something started → preterite empezaron.

turns.why: Usted with patients, present tense for a current symptom, and it separates exertion from rest.

turns.es: Cuando camino, y también en la noche. No puedo dormir acostado.
turns.en: When I walk, and also at night. I can't sleep lying flat.

turns.es: Me duelen mucho las pantorrillas, y cuando descanso se me quita.

turns.es: No, pero sudé mucho y me faltaba el aire.
turns.en: No, but I sweated a lot and I was short of breath.

items.title: A daughter worried about her mother

turns.es: Doctor, mi mamá tiene los pies muy hinchados.
turns.en: Doctor, my mom's feet are very swollen.

opts: ¿Desde cuándo tuvo los pies hinchados mañana?
turns.why: Asking about the mother (she → tiene), present tense with desde cuándo.

turns.es: Desde hace dos semanas. Y en la noche no puede dormir acostada.
turns.en: For two weeks. And at night she can't sleep lying flat.

opts: ¿Cuántas almohadas usa su mamá para dormir?
¿Cuántas almohadas usa tu mamá para dormir?
turns.why: Usted with the family (su mamá); almohada is feminine (cuántas).

turns.es: Tres, y a veces se despierta con falta de aire.
turns.en: Three, and sometimes she wakes up short of breath.

opts: ¿Tu mamá se cansa más que antes?
¿Su mamá se cansa más que antes al caminar?
¿Su mamá se cansaba más que antes mañana?
turns.why: Usted (su mamá), present tense, comparing with before.

turns.es: Sí, ya casi no camina. Se cansa mucho.
turns.en: Yes, she hardly walks anymore. She gets very tired.

roleplay.title: Breathless and swollen
roleplay.setup: You are the cardiologist seeing a new patient referred for shortness of breath. Find out when he gets short of breath, how he sleeps, whether he has swelling, and how far he can walk now compared with before.
roleplay.persona: You are José Martínez, 68, originally from Michoacán, Mexico, living in Chicago for 30 years, retired from restaurant work. Over the last two or three months you have gotten short of breath more and more easily. Facts: you used to walk about ten blocks to church; now you stop after one block because of breathlessness (not pain). You now sleep with three pillows and sometimes in the armchair. Two or three nights a week you wake up suddenly short of breath and have to sit up. Your ankles and feet swell, worse in the afternoon; your shoes feel tight. You get tired easily. No chest pain, no fainting, no palpitations. Speak simple Mexican Spanish at an intermediate level: present, preterite and imperfect, short sentences, everyday words (cuadras, almohadas, me falta el aire, se me hinchan los pies). Use usted with the doctor. Answer only what is asked; reveal the night-time waking and the swelling only if the doctor asks about sleep at night or about the feet/legs. If the doctor uses tú, answer normally but sound slightly surprised.
roleplay.opening: Buenas tardes, doctor. Vengo porque me canso mucho y me falta el aire.
goals: Ask whether the breathlessness comes with exertion, at rest, or lying down
Find out how many pillows he uses to sleep
Ask whether he wakes up at night short of breath
Ask about swelling of the feet or ankles and when it is worse
Compare how many blocks he can walk now versus before

roleplay.title: A faint at church
roleplay.setup: You are the electrophysiologist seeing a woman who fainted three days ago. Get the full fainting history: the setting, warning signs, how long she was out, injuries, and what the witness saw.
roleplay.persona: You are Rosa Pérez, 55, from Guatemala, living in Chicago, works cleaning offices. Three days ago you fainted at a long Sunday Mass: the church was very hot and crowded and you had been standing for a long time. Before fainting you felt hot, sweaty, nauseated, and your vision went dim. You fell and hit your left elbow (bruised, not broken); you did not hit your head. Your daughter saw it and says you were out for a few seconds, you looked very pale, and you woke up quickly and knew where you were. You did not lose control of your bladder and did not bite your tongue. No palpitations or chest pain before. You fainted once before as a teenager, also standing in a hot place. Speak simple Spanish at an intermediate level: present, preterite and imperfect, short sentences. Use usted with the doctor. Answer only what is asked; do not volunteer the earlier faint or the elbow injury unless asked about past episodes or injuries.
roleplay.opening: Doctor, el domingo me desmayé en la iglesia y mi hija se asustó mucho.
goals: Find out what she was doing and where she was when she fainted
Ask what she felt before the faint (warning signs)
Ask how long she was unconscious and how she was when she woke up
Ask whether she hit her head or got hurt
Ask whether anyone saw it and whether it has happened before
